questions.question: Why compute Cohen's kappa instead of relying only on raw agreement?
options: Raw agreement flatters a judge when most outputs pass; kappa corrects for chance agreement
questions.explanation: With mostly-PASS data, high raw agreement can occur by chance, so kappa gives a fairer measure of judge reliability.

questions.question: What is the purpose of swapping positions in pairwise comparison?
options: To counter judges favouring whichever answer appears first
questions.explanation: Running each pair in both orders and counting a win only when both agree reduces position bias.

questions.question: Prompt v2 scored 88% against v1's 84% on 200 cases, and the 95% bootstrap interval was -0.5% to +9.0%. What does this indicate?
options: The test set is too small to run
The evidence is not conclusive because the interval includes zero
questions.explanation: An interval that includes zero means the gap could be noise; the lesson also notes v2 broke 8 cases v1 passed.

questions.question: Why split a rubric into one criterion per judge call?
options: A judge scoring several criteria at once tends to blur them; separate binary calls are easier to calibrate and debug
The API only allows one criterion
It removes the need for humans
questions.explanation: Separate PASS/FAIL calls per criterion are easier to calibrate and debug than one blended score.
